entry.name: MIT 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
entry.note: MIT's annual bootcamp; every January's lectures posted free with labs

reading.format: Course; concludes with a project proposal competition with feedback from staff and industry sponsors.
reading.summary: This is MIT's introductory course on deep learning methods and applications. It covers natural language processing, computer vision, biology, and more. Students gain foundational knowledge of deep learning algorithms, practical experience building neural networks, and understanding of cutting-edge topics including large language models and generative AI. The program concludes with a project proposal competition with feedback from staff and industry sponsors.
reading.audience: The page indicates it is for students with calculus and linear algebra background, though Python experience is helpful but not necessary. Listeners are also welcome.
reading.prerequisites: Calculus (taking derivatives) and linear algebra (matrix multiplication) are assumed. Experience in Python is helpful but not necessary.
